item.content:encoded:
News / NewsBTC / Fusionist ACE Bridge Exploit: $5.7M Loss Estimate, Bithumb Freezes Trading

Fusionist ACE Bridge Exploit: $5.7M Loss Estimate, Bithumb Freezes Trading 5 min read

ACEUSD ACE Key takeaways The Fusionist ACE bridge exploit is estimated at $5.7 million across two stages, according to SlowMist, which is not an audited final total. About $1.87 million in proceeds was traced to the attacker, while 53.7 million genuine ACE tokens, valued near $3.7 million, were reportedly withdrawn through the bridge. Bithumb halted ACE trading on November 23 after finding signs that abnormally issued ACE had entered exchanges. In the material reviewed, Fusionist has not published a reconciled loss figure or a technical post-mortem. The Fusionist ACE bridge exploit has produced an estimated $5.7 million in losses across two stages, according to SlowMist’s incident tracker. After unbacked ACE tokens were minted on BNB Chain and sold, traders reportedly used the resulting price collapse to withdraw real ACE from the project’s Endurance bridge reserves. The fallout reached centralized exchanges on Monday, November 23: Bithumb halted ACE trading after finding indications that abnormally issued tokens had entered crypto exchanges. This was not one attacker walking away with $5.7 million in a single transaction. The distinction matters. Roughly $1.87 million was traced through the attacker’s proceeds, while another 53.7 million genuine ACE tokens, valued around $3.7 million at the incident’s reference prices, were reportedly withdrawn through the bridge. SlowMist lists a combined $5.7 million loss estimate, not an audited final total. The bridge’s most basic promise, that a token issued on one chain corresponds to something real on another, is precisely what now needs proving. A Privileged Minter Printed Tokens That Had No Backing Security firm Blockaid flagged the Fusionist bridge-minter exploit on November 22. Its alert described the mechanism bluntly: “ A privileged token-bridge minter minted unbacked ACE and sold it for USDT. Blockaid · November 22 alert The firm initially estimated that about $1.04 million had been extracted while the attack was still ongoing. That was an interim snapshot, not a cap on the damage.

Blockchain-monitoring account Onchain Lens subsequently reported that an attacker had routed 1,091.5 ETH, valued at about $1.87 million at the time, through Tornado Cash. That observation traces a movement of proceeds, not an extra $1.87 million to add on top of the initial extraction estimate. The values describe different points in the same suspected attacker’s fund flow.

Fusionist acknowledged an apparent ongoing ACE exploit on BNB Smart Chain on Sunday and asked users to suspend transfers, trading and bridging on that network. It has not, in the material reviewed, provided a reconciled loss figure or a technical post-mortem identifying how the privileged minting authority was abused. A bridge minter is supposed to create a token representation only when the corresponding value is properly accounted for. Once the right to mint is misused, a chain can show perfectly ordinary-looking balances that have no matching backing. It is a familiar failure mode: NewsBTC previously covered a bridge-role exploit that minted unbacked tokens at CrediX. That earlier case does not establish Fusionist’s root cause, but it illustrates why elevated bridge permissions are such a consequential security boundary. Traders Found a Second Exit Through Real ACE Reserves The subsequent drain may prove more important than the initial minting spree. According to SlowMist’s November 22 incident entry, traders bought the sharply discounted ACE created by the market disruption and used the cross-chain bridge to withdraw about 53.7 million genuine ACE from the Endurance-side reserves. SlowMist valued that withdrawal at approximately $3.7 million. Here is the mechanism without the jargon. A representation of ACE on BNB Chain suddenly became cheap because unauthorized supply had flooded the market. A bridge that would still accept those tokens in exchange for ACE on Endurance offered an obvious difference in value. Anyone able to complete that conversion could receive real tokens in return for deeply discounted ones. The trading opportunity existed because the backing and the circulating representation were no longer in a trustworthy relationship. The $3.7 million figure is a valuation of the ACE reserve outflow, not proof that every recipient sold those tokens for $3.7 million in cash. Nor does it mean every trader involved helped compromise the minter. There is a meaningful difference between initiating the security breach and trading through a system whose defenses have already failed. Those distinctions should not obscure the core problem. A bridge can have technically valid transactions and still produce an economically disastrous result. If unbacked supply can be redeemed for genuine reserves, the checks have failed where they matter most. Bithumb’s Monday Halt Shows How Far the Problem Travelled Bithumb suspended ACE deposits and withdrawals early on November 23. It then halted trading effective 7:30 a.m. Korea time , according to its follow-up ACE security notice. The exchange said, in a translation from its Korean announcement, that it had: “ confirmed indications that abnormally issued ACE had entered cryptocurrency exchanges. Bithumb · ACE security notice It identified two related BNB Chain transactions and a second transaction. Those records are important evidence leads, but a full independent decoding of the transaction trail remains outstanding. Bithumb’s wording is careful: it reported signs of abnormal supply entering exchanges, not a finding that every ACE token in customer accounts is invalid. The trading suspension is a protective response, not a finalized determination of customer losses. Still, it creates a practical problem for holders who never used the bridge. If tokens are fungible within a market, exchanges and the issuer need a credible method for identifying affected supply and deciding how deposits, balances and trades will be treated. The Real Security Question Is Why the Bridge Could Honor the Claims There is an understandable temptation to focus on the enormous minting figures. The more consequential question is what happened when those tokens met the bridge’s reserves. A system does not need to lose control of its entire blockchain to suffer a serious failure in one privileged contract role. Nor should a successful-looking bridge transaction count as evidence that the asset being transferred was fully backed.Our assessment The response cannot end with a pause notice and a promise to investigate. Fusionist needs to show which minting permissions were affected, whether they have been revoked, how much ACE was created without backing, how the Endurance-side reserve changed and what claims remain outstanding. Exchanges need a defensible token-treatment plan, and holders need to know whether there is a shortfall and who is responsible for covering it. There is a fair counterargument: the $5.7 million figure is an external estimate, market prices moved during the incident, and the precise compromise method is not established. SlowMist categorizes the incident as private-key leakage, but that classification is not a substitute for an official technical finding. It would also be premature to treat a cautious exchange halt as proof that every affected customer suffered a loss. Those qualifications change how the numbers should be reported. They do not make the underlying bridge-accounting failure less serious. The next credible milestone is not a restored interface or a reassuring social post. It is a transparent reconciliation of the tokens minted, the reserves withdrawn and the assets still available to back legitimate ACE claims. Until that exists, the estimated $5.7 million fallout remains a warning about both token security and the risks of trusting a bridge’s accounting. item.content:encoded:
News / Crypto Briefing / Solana ETFs post $4.38 million weekly inflow as Bitcoin, Ether and XRP funds bleed

Solana ETFs post $4.38 million weekly inflow as Bitcoin, Ether and XRP funds bleed 1 min read

SOLUSD US spot Solana ETFs pulled in $4.38 million in net inflows last week. Spot ETFs tracking Bitcoin, Ether and XRP all posted net outflows over the same stretch. It is the first time in seven weeks that SOL funds finished a week in the green. The inflow came during the trading week of November 16 to 20, 2026. It broke a run of six consecutive weekly outflows for the SOL products. Those six losing weeks were costly. Combined net withdrawals over that period came to about $197 million. Bitwise's BSOL did most of the heavy lifting. The fund took in roughly $6.08 million on the week, more than the category's entire net total. Fidelity's FSOL logged the largest outflow among the SOL funds, at approximately $1.20 million. Daily flows were choppy. Monday, November 16, delivered a $11.7 million inflow, and several outflow days followed later in the week before the tally settled at a modest net positive. The price action was calm by crypto standards. SOL traded in a range between $70 and $73 during the inflow period. Total assets under management for US spot SOL ETFs sat at around $965 million as of November 20. That works out to about 2.42% of Solana's market capitalization. Since launch, the SOL funds have collected cumulative net inflows estimated somewhere between $1.41 billion and $1.65 billion. The contrast with the larger crypto ETFs is what made this week stand out. Spot funds for Bitcoin, Ether and XRP all recorded net outflows in the latest reported weeks. Bitcoin took the hardest hit. Some reports put weekly BTC ETF outflows at more than $1 billion. Ether and XRP funds also saw money leave. Combined with Bitcoin, that left SOL as the odd one out among the major spot crypto ETFs tracked for the week. One fund, BSOL, accounted for more than the entire net inflow, while FSOL lost money. That concentration means the turnaround leaned heavily on demand for a single issuer's product rather than broad buying across the category. SOL ETF assets of around $965 million are a fraction of what flows through Bitcoin products in a single heavy week, so SOL fund flows are unlikely to move the overall ETF picture on their own.

News / Stock Story / Earnings to watch: Movado reports Q3 results tomorrow

Earnings to watch: Movado reports Q3 results tomorrow 1 min read

MOV

Luxury watch company Movado MOV will be reporting results this Tuesday before market open. Here’s what you need to know. Movado beat analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $169.8 million, up 4.9% year on year. It was a very strong quarter for the company, with a beat of analysts’ EPS estimates. Is Movado a buy or sell going into earnings? Read our full analysis here, it’s free for active Edge members . This quarter, the market is expecting Movado’s revenue to grow 5% year on year, improving from the 3.1% increase it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. Movado has missed Wall Street’s revenue estimates multiple times over the last two years. Looking at Movado’s peers in the consumer discretionary - apparel and accessories segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. Figs delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 25.7%, beating analysts’ expectations by 4.4%, and VF Corp reported revenues up 1.2%, topping estimates by 1.1%. Figs traded down 1.9% following the results while VF Corp was up 7.6%. Read our full analysis of Figs’s results here and VF Corp’s results here . Investors in the consumer discretionary - apparel and accessories segment have had fairly steady hands going into earnings, with share prices down 1.1% on average over the last month. Movado is down 5.5% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $47.50 (compared to the current share price of $29.25).
